description:
AI Answer Copier is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that solves the "Final Mile" friction in educational content creation. It enables AI models to move beyond just writing questions to actually generating the files required for teaching and assessment.

By functioning as a native MCP server, this tool allows Claude or any MCP-enabled IDE to directly pipe its output into specialized educational formats. No more manually fixing bullet points in Word or wrestling with CSV headers for your LMS.

Key Capabilities:Zero-Friction Pipeline: Your AI can now "see" your local export tools. Ask it to: "Generate 10 biology questions and send them directly to my Quizizz CSV."

Multi-Format Exporting: Seamlessly convert AI responses into upload-ready files for Kahoot, Quizizz, Canvas (JSON), Moodle (XML), and professionally formatted PDFs.

Intelligent Smart-Parse: Automatically identifies question stems, multiple-choice distractors, and correct answer keys from raw AI text.

First-Class Math & Code: Native support for LaTeX equations ($\sqrt{x}$) and indented code snippets (Python/C++), ensuring they don't break during the export

Why use this MCP server? Generating questions takes seconds, but formatting them takes hours. This server reclaims those 5 hours of your week by removing the technical barrier between AI intelligence and classroom delivery.

code_style.description: Syntax highlighting theme for fenced code blocks in HTML, PDF, and image output.

html_theme.description: Visual theme for HTML/PDF/PNG output. 'light' = white background, 'dark' = dark background.

pdf_margin.description: PDF margin in CSS units, applied to all sides. Examples: '20mm', '1in', '0.5cm'.

default_title.description: Fallback document title when none is provided. Used in PDF metadata, HTML title, XML root.

max_input_bytes.description: Max input size in bytes. Documents exceeding this are rejected. Default: 1 GB (1073741824).

pdf_page_format.description: Paper size for PDF output. Controls page dimensions for Markdown-to-PDF conversion.

tool_signatures.name: analyze_document
tool_signatures.description: Analyze Markdown and return comprehensive statistics: line/word/character/paragraph/sentence counts, heading/code/table/link/image counts, and estimated reading time.

markdown.description: The Markdown text to analyze.

tool_signatures.name: batch_convert
tool_signatures.description: Batch-convert multiple Markdown documents to one or more output formats in a single call. Accepts an array of items (each with markdown content and optional title) and an array of target format IDs. Supports 22 formats: txt, csv, json, xml, xlsx, latex, rtf, docx, pdf, html, md, email, slack, discord, jira, confluence, asciidoc, rst, mediawiki, bbcode, textile, orgmode. Errors are isolated per item+format so one failure does not stop the rest. When output_dir is provided, files are written to disk; otherwise binary formats are returned as base64 and text formats inline. Returns a summary (total_conversions, successful, failed) plus per-item results.

title.description: Optional. Document title used in PDF metadata, HTML title, XML root element.

markdown.description: The Markdown source text to convert.

items.description: Array of documents to convert. Each item must have a 'markdown' string and an optional 'title' string.

formats.description: Array of output format IDs to convert each item into. Valid values: txt, csv, json, xml, xlsx, latex, rtf, docx, pdf, html, md, email, slack, discord, jira, confluence, asciidoc, rst, mediawiki, bbcode, textile, orgmode.

output_dir.description: Optional. Directory path where converted files will be saved. Created automatically if it does not exist. When omitted, results are returned inline.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_asciidoc
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to AsciiDoc format with = headers, ---- code blocks, url[text] links, and image:: directives.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_bbcode
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to BBCode format with [b], [i], [code], [url], [img] tags for phpBB/vBulletin forums.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_confluence
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to Confluence wiki markup with {info}, {note} panels and {code:language=x} syntax.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_csv
tool_signatures.description: Extract tables from Markdown and convert them to CSV format. Parses GFM pipe-tables from the input and outputs comma-separated values. Non-table content is ignored.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text containing tables.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_discord
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to Discord-compatible format with styled bold/underline headers and preserved code blocks.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_docx
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to a Microsoft Word DOCX file. Produces a binary .docx document with styled headings, bold/italic text, numbered and bulleted lists, and code formatting. Binary format — output_path should almost always be provided.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the binary .docx file.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_email_html
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to email-optimized HTML with all styles inlined, compatible with Outlook, Gmail, and Apple Mail.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_html
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to a complete, styled HTML document. Renders GFM (tables, task lists, strikethrough) and KaTeX math into semantic HTML with an embedded stylesheet.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_image
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to a PNG image. Renders the Markdown as styled HTML (GFM tables, KaTeX math) and takes a full-page screenshot via a headless Chromium browser. Binary format — output_path should almost always be provided.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the binary .png file.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_jira
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to JIRA wiki markup with h1./h2. headings, {code} blocks, and [text|url] links.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_json
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to a structured JSON representation. Parses the document into a JSON object with sections, headings, paragraphs, lists, code blocks, and tables.

title.description: Optional. A document title string. Defaults to 'document' if omitted.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_latex
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to LaTeX source code. Produces a LaTeX document fragment with \section, \textbf, \textit, list environments, verbatim code blocks, and table environments. KaTeX math expressions are passed through as native LaTeX math.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_md
tool_signatures.description: Export Markdown content, optionally harmonizing its formatting first. When harmonize=false (default), returns the input unchanged. When harmonize=true, applies normalization.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to export.

harmonize.description: Optional. When true, normalizes Markdown syntax before returning or saving. Defaults to false.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_mediawiki
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to MediaWiki markup with == headers, '''bold''', <syntaxhighlight> tags, and {| wikitable syntax.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_orgmode
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to Emacs Org Mode format with * headers, #+BEGIN_SRC/#+END_SRC code, and [[url][text]] links.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_pdf
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to a PDF document. Renders the Markdown as styled HTML (GFM tables, KaTeX math) and prints it to PDF via a headless Chromium browser. Binary format — output_path should almost always be provided.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the binary .pdf file.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_rst
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to reStructuredText (RST) format with underlined headers, .. code-block:: directives, and RST reference syntax.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_rtf
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to Rich Text Format (RTF). Produces an RTF document string preserving basic formatting: bold, italic, headers, lists, and code blocks.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_slack
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to Slack mrkdwn format. Bold as *, links as <url|text>, headers as bold text.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_textile
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to Textile markup format for Redmine, Basecamp, and CMS platforms.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_txt
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to plain text by stripping all formatting — removes headers, bold/italic markers, links, images, code fences, and HTML tags. The result is a human-readable plain-text string with no markup.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_xlsx
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown tables to a Microsoft Excel XLSX spreadsheet. Each table becomes a sheet in the workbook. Non-table content is ignored. Binary format — output_path should almost always be provided.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text containing tables.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the binary .xlsx file.

tool_signatures.name: convert_to_xml
tool_signatures.description: Convert Markdown to an XML document. Produces well-formed XML with an <?xml?> declaration and structured elements including section, heading, paragraph, list, code, and table.

title.description: Optional. The root XML element name and document title. Defaults to 'document' if omitted.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: extract_code_blocks
tool_signatures.description: Extract all code blocks from Markdown. Returns JSON array with language, code content, and start/end line numbers.

markdown.description: The Markdown text to extract code blocks from.

tool_signatures.name: extract_links
tool_signatures.description: Extract all links and images from Markdown. Returns JSON with text, URL, line number, and type (inline, reference, image, autolink).

markdown.description: The Markdown text to extract links from.

tool_signatures.name: extract_structure
tool_signatures.description: Extract full document structure overview: statistics, heading outline, code block summary, and link summary.

markdown.description: The Markdown text to extract structure from.

tool_signatures.name: generate_html
tool_signatures.description: Generate a complete, self-contained HTML document from Markdown with all styles inlined. Returns the HTML string directly — no file is written to disk. This tool is read-only and performs no file I/O.

title.description: Optional. Sets the <title> tag in the HTML document's <head> section. Defaults to 'Document' if omitted.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert.

tool_signatures.name: generate_toc
tool_signatures.description: Generate a Markdown Table of Contents from headings with configurable max_depth (1-6) and indented links.

markdown.description: The Markdown text to generate a TOC from.

tool_signatures.name: harmonize_markdown
tool_signatures.description: Standardize and normalize Markdown syntax without changing the document's meaning. Re-formats headers (ATX-style), normalizes list markers to '-', enforces fenced code blocks with backticks, and applies consistent indentation. Side effects: when output_path is provided, writes the harmonized Markdown to disk. When output_path is omitted, returns the harmonized text as a string with no file I/O.

markdown.description: The raw Markdown source text to convert. Supports GitHub-Flavored Markdown (tables, task lists, strikethrough) and KaTeX math expressions. Pass the full document content as a string, not a file path.

output_path.description: Optional. Absolute or relative file path where the result will be saved. Parent directories are created automatically. If omitted, the converted text content is returned directly.

tool_signatures.name: html_to_markdown
tool_signatures.description: Convert HTML content (full document or fragment) back to Markdown. Handles headings, tables, lists, code blocks, links, images, and inline formatting.

html.description: The HTML content to convert to Markdown.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.

tool_signatures.name: lint_markdown
tool_signatures.description: Lint Markdown and report issues as a JSON array with line number, severity, rule name, message, and fixable flag.

markdown.description: The Markdown text to lint.

tool_signatures.name: repair_markdown
tool_signatures.description: Repair broken Markdown from LLM output or copy-paste. Fixes unclosed code fences, broken tables, stray emphasis markers, missing heading spaces, and broken links.

markdown.description: The potentially broken Markdown text to repair.

output_path.description: Optional. File path to save the result.
